title: Partner Co-sell Pipeline Review - Orchid Partners
summary: Quarterly co-sell pipeline review. Reviewed joint opportunities, prioritized three near-term deals for joint pursuit, discussed technical POC requirements for a retail customer, and aligned on next steps for co-marketing and deal ownership. Partner asked clarifications around dedicated vs hosted for regulated customers; SE committed to run a short benchmark. Action items assigned.

Daniel to coordinate co-marketing case study template and draft by 2026-02-28

transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-02-14
Time: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Lena Ortiz (Redwood AE), Marcus Chen (Redwood SE), Daniel Park (Redwood Partnerships), Priya Nair (Orchid Head of Alliances), Tom Reyes (Orchid Partner Sales), Aisha Khan (Orchid Solutions Architect)
Recording ID: ff-2026-02-14-orchid-001

Summary Notes (auto): Quick run-through of 7 active co-sell opportunities, deep dive on RetailCo POC, clarification on dedicated vs hosted for regulated data, next steps assigned.

Transcript:
[00:00] Lena: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you making time on Valentine's Day, we will keep this tight, quick pipeline review and then dive into RetailCo POC.
[00:12] Priya: Thanks Lena, happy to be here. Quick note, Tom has a hard stop at 10:40 for another meeting.
[00:18] Marcus: Great, I'll try to keep technical bits short early then we can follow up with a separate deep dive if needed.
[00:24] Tom: Sounds good.
[00:26] Lena: Ok first slide, current co-sell pipeline — we have seven active deals. Two are in discovery, three in demo/poc, and two are late-stage. Main ones I want to flag are RetailCo (POC), FinSolve (expansion), and MedSys (procurement/legal stage).
[00:44] Priya: Can you remind us of the value props we're leaning on for RetailCo? I remember latency and cost were big for them.
[00:51] Lena: Yes correct — RetailCo cares about latency for real-time recommendations and cost per inference at scale. Also data residency and audit logs because they handle payment data.
[01:05] Marcus: From a technical perspective we proposed a dedicated Redwood Dedicated pool for predictable throughput, plus optional private deployment for a subset of functions that must remain in their VPC. There was some back-and-forth on whether a hosted VPC option could satisfy their compliance team.
[01:22] Aisha: Right, our infra team asked if the hosted option supports customer-managed KMS — they said earlier it was not, but we heard Redwood had KMS integrations?
[01:31] Marcus: We do support KMS integrations and customer-managed keys for Private deployments; for Hosted API there's envelope encryption but not full KMS tenancy. That said, for many customers we do dedicated with VPC peering which gives strong isolation. Sorry if earlier notes were fuzzy, transcription sometimes mixes terms.
[01:49] Tom: So for RetailCo, without on-prem, they may accept dedicated with VPC peer and CMK. That keeps it simpler than a full Private install.
[01:58] Priya: Timeline — RetailCo wants a POC in 3 weeks, they want to show results to their board in early April. Is that realistic?
[02:08] Marcus: For a basic throughput and latency POC we can do 2-3 weeks if we have dev access and a small dataset. The main time sink is data transfers and legal approvals for test data.
[02:21] Lena: Okay for responsibilities — Marcus to own benchmark plan, Orchid to provide test dataset and infra contacts, Lena to coordinate commercial terms for POC.
[02:29] Tom: Quick question on pricing — are we expecting Redwood to bill the POC usage or Orchid? Need clarity for procurement.
[02:35] Lena: Typically Redwood bills the usage for hosted POCs; for Dedicated we often do a short-term reserved or a trial credit. We'll put options in the co-sell one-pager.
[02:45] Priya: Good.
[02:47] Marcus: I want to call out one technical risk — RetailCo uses very long context windows for session logs, which can blow up RAM/KV cache sizes. We recommend a quantized model variant and prefix caching to keep costs predictable.
[03:04] Aisha: Do you have examples of model variants that perform well? Anything Redwood-verified?
[03:09] Marcus: Yes we have a catalog of verified models with performance profiles, I'll include the relevant ones in the benchmark plan. There may be slight name mismatches in docs — sometimes the model alias differs.
[03:20] Daniel: On the co-marketing side, Priya, we discussed a joint case study with RetailCo if the POC is successful, is Orchid comfortable leading outreach?
[03:28] Priya: Yes, we'll coordinate PR and customer approval. Daniel, can you share the case study template?
[03:33] Daniel: Absolutely, I'll send a draft.
[03:36] Tom: Shifting to FinSolve — quick update, they want embed search for compliance documents, and they've asked about on-prem options due to regs.
[03:46] Lena: For FinSolve we proposed Redwood Private for a subset and hosted for non-sensitive workloads. It's a hybrid ask.
[03:54] Marcus: That hybrid is feasible; we'll need to capture network requirements and cert needs early.
[04:01] Tom: Ok makes sense.
[04:03] Priya: Any competitor pressure on FinSolve?
[04:06] Lena: They evaluated CloudVendorX and Anthropic earlier; CloudVendorX pushed a lower-cost but less integrated solution. We should emphasize our observability and rollout controls.
[04:17] Aisha: For the POC test plan, what metrics should we capture? Latency p95, cost per 1k tokens, throughput, and model accuracy on the prompt set?
[04:27] Marcus: Yes, and also memory/KV cache usage, and a reproducible prompt set for regression testing. We'll include trace samples for top slow requests.
[04:37] Tom: Quick halftime check — we are moving a bit long, Tom (Orchid) has the hard stop at 10:40. Should we go straight to RetailCo POC scoping?
[04:46] Lena: Yes, let's focus on RetailCo.
[04:48] Marcus: POC scope: 1) Baseline latency/throughput for real-time recs, 2) Validate quantized model variant accuracy against their labeled test set, 3) Exercise KV cache and prefix caching to measure cost savings, 4) Security review for KMS and audit logs. Is that aligned?
[05:04] Priya: Yes aligned.
[05:06] Aisha: On data — RetailCo can provide a sanitized slice of session logs and anonymized payment-metadata. Legal will need to review, but we can get a subset quickly.
[05:16] Marcus: Great, I'll prepare an ingestion script and minimal schema for them. If we get a small sample by Friday we can run week-of-mock tests.
[05:26] Tom: For the dedicated sizing, what GPU types are you recommending? G and H or something else?
[05:31] Marcus: For this workload we recommend A100-style or comparable M-Class with larger memory for long contexts; but we can run the benchmark on more cost-efficient instances if latency targets are moderate. We'll include cost/loss tradeoffs in the plan.
[05:45] Priya: Will you include an estimate for token cost per 1M requests? RetailCo wants a ballpark.
[05:52] Lena: Yes, Marcus will provide cost modeling with two scenarios: aggressive latency SLAs and a cost-optimized config.
[05:59] Marcus: Note there may be a 10-15% variance depending on cache hit rates. I'll show a sensitivity table.
[06:08] Daniel: Any legal blockers on sharing benchmark infra diagrams with RetailCo?
[06:12] Lena: We can share a high-level architecture and non-sensitive metrics; detailed infra diagrams are only shared under NDA or later in the process.
[06:21] Tom: Ok that's fine.
[06:23] Priya: Switching quick to ownership on the three late-stage deals — who will be primary contact?
[06:27] Lena: For MedSys, Redwood AE (Lena) is primary with Orchid sales (Tom) as co-sell. For FinSolve, Priya will lead with Redwood support. For RetailCo, joint ownership during POC, then we'll propose a primary owner post-POC.
[06:44] Tom: Quick ask — can Redwood provide a short contract template for a POC that Orchid can use when we manage the billing? Cuts down legal back-and-forth.
[06:53] Lena: Yes we have a standard co-sell POC addendum; I'll attach it to the one-pager.
[06:59] Aisha: Technical cliff notes — any limitations around function/tool calling? RetailCo wants to call an internal inventory service during generation to re-rank results.
[07:08] Marcus: We support function/tool calling patterns; for Private and Dedicated you can host the tool endpoint in the VPC. For Hosted we have limited direct network calls, so we'd recommend Dedicated with VPC access for real-time calls.
[07:25] Aisha: Good to know.
[07:28] Lena: Ok we are at ~25 minutes in; Tom you have to drop soon — any final concerns?
[07:33] Tom: The only thing is procurement — Orchid needs a clear commercial split if we bring the deal in. Do we have guidance?
[07:40] Lena: We usually negotiate a reseller margin for partner-led deals; I'll include a recommended split and the eligibility criteria in the deck. If it's joint-sourced, we can discuss a referral or commission model.
[07:52] Priya: That will help.
[07:54] Marcus: One more technical note — we should run a small scale stress test (10k concurrent sessions) to validate autoscaling before Prod. I can include a recommended stress harness.
[08:04] Aisha: We'll get infra contacts for that.
[08:07] Tom: Perfect. I have to jump now, thanks all.
[08:10] Tom: Bye.
[08:13] (Tom drops)
[08:15] Lena: Ok continuing, Marcus can you walk through the benchmark plan milestones?
[08:20] Marcus: Sure — Week 0: align on dataset and access, Week 1: baseline runs and model variant comparisons, Week 2: caching and optimization runs, Week 3: wrap-up and final report. I'll attach scripts and expected artifacts. We expect to deliver a performance brief and cost model.
[08:35] Priya: For instrumentation, can you include tracing pointers we can share with their SRE team?
[08:40] Marcus: Yes, we'll include tracing sample IDs and how to instrument the SDK.
[08:44] Lena: Any risk flags we haven't covered?
[08:47] Aisha: Potential delay is legal for test data, otherwise good.
[08:51] Priya: Also need to check data residency requirements for EU customers — Redwood do you have EU regions available?
[08:58] Marcus: Yes we have EU hosted regions and we can place Dedicated capacity in EU; for Private we can on-prem. I'll note region availability in the plan.
[09:08] Daniel: Co-marketing — we'll aim to have a joint press guard rails doc ready if POC goes well.
[09:14] Priya: Sounds good.
[09:16] Lena: Ok quick recap of owners and dates: Lena send one-pager by 2/16, Marcus benchmark plan by 2/20, Priya share RFP by 2/18, Daniel co-marketing draft by 2/28. Anything else?
[09:29] Aisha: No.
[09:30] Lena: Great thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email and set the benchmark kickoff meeting.
[09:36] (Meeting ends)

Notes about transcript quality: occasional misattribution (e.g., sometimes system labeled Redwood as "Speaker 2" in raw export), some words mistranscribed (KMS as "KMS integrations" ok but sometimes shows as "K-M-S"), punctuation inconsistent.
